text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London retained most of their losses by the close. September lost $30 to close at $1,641 per tonne. November gave up $32 to close at $1,630 per tonne. A report that Brazilian production in 1997/98 (April/May) is officially seen to reach 20 million bags, down from the 22 million bags forecast by the Industry and Commerce Ministry earlier this year, failed to stir the market, especially as Roberto Abreu, the interim head of the National Coffee Department, said that the government sticks to its 22 million bag forecast. Predictions for the 1997/98 coffee crop have ranged widely from 18 million bags to the USDA's estimate of 28 million bags. Many recent Brazilian trade forecasts have come in at around 23-25 million bags.

Arabica futures in New York ended mixed in choppy dealings with much of the day's focus centered on the nearby September/December switch. September lost 1.25 cents/lb to close at 184.50 cents/lb while December added 1.20 cents/lb to close at 162.55 cents/lb. The market showed no reaction to a forecast by independent Brazilian meteorologist Somar that the country's coffee producing areas are likely to escape frost at the end of next week as a cold front heading for the region will be tempered by low pressure systems. However, it was added that it was still too early to completely exclude the prospect of frost and that forecasters would continue to closely monitor the situation. Weather forecaster Cropcast earlier said its latest long-range guidance models continue to show a 20 per cent probability of a freeze in Brazil's coffee belt next week.
UNITED STATES - The CSCE reported certified coffee stocks fell by 250 60-kg bags as of July 30, to 92,399 bags. An additional 750 bags were pending grading, the Exchange said.

BRAZIL - The Brazilian soluble industry can import coffee if it wants, Industry and Commerce Minister Francisco Dornelles recently said. However, the proposal to lend stocks to the soluble industry, recently trumpeted as a done deal, has apparently come unstuck as the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and the Finance Ministry battle over it. Brazilian soluble coffee exports totalled 386,000 60-kg bags in the first half of 1997, a drop of 17.5 per cent from the 468,000 bags shipped the same period last year. Soluble producers said the main reasons for Brazil's loss of competitiveness were the higher cost of raw materials for the soluble industry compared with other countries and heavy European Union taxes on imports of Brazilian soluble coffee. To lower costs for raw materials the Brazilian soluble industry plans to import coffee.

SINGAPORE ** - Singapore imported 215,800 bags of coffee in January/February 1997, 13 per cent less than was imported the same two months the previous year. The largest supplier of green coffee in January/February 1997 was Vietnam with 124,700 bags, up from 49,800 bags shipped the same two months in 1996.

The country exported 243,200 bags of coffee in January/February 1997, 16 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1996. The main market for green coffee in January/February 1997 was Algeria (50,000 vs 83,300 bags), while the bulk of solubles was shipped to the Russian Federation (33,900 vs 43,500 bags).
